public_rationale: Marcus's main claim is a broad judgment that the 'cognitive capacities' of LLMs are 'severely limited'. He names no task, model, measure or threshold. The resolution contract finds no agreed standard for that phrase. One of his stated reasons is that LLMs cannot fact-check their own work. An ICLR 2024 paper, in a version dated 14 March 2024, reports that LLMs struggle to correct their own reasoning without external feedback. It also reports that their performance sometimes gets worse after self-correction (e1). OpenAI's GPT-4 Technical Report was first released in March 2023, and its cited version is dated 4 March 2024. It says GPT-4 is less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios. It also says GPT-4 shows human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks, including a simulated bar exam score around the top 10% of test takers (e2). Whether these findings amount to 'severely limited' depends on a standard the claim does not give. So the claim cannot be scored as supported or contradicted.
limitations: e1 covers only intrinsic self-correction on reasoning tasks. It does not test hallucination rates or 'cognitive capacity' in general.
e1 reports that LLMs 'struggle' to self-correct. It does not show whether that amounts to the 'utter inability' in Marcus's wording.
e2 covers a single model, GPT-4. It is the developer's own disclosure, not an independent evaluation.
The narrower premises (errors, hallucinations, weak self-checking) were not graded separately.
The evidence packet has only two items, and both are context. Neither tests the broad judgment directly.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs' cognitive capacities are severely limited, as shown by their errors, hallucinations, and inability to fact-check their own work.
conditions: evidenced by boneheaded errors, hallucinations, and inability to fact-check their own work

statement.excerpt: For a long time I have been baffled about why so many people take LLMs so seriously, when it is obvious, from the boneheaded errors, hallucinations, and utter inability to fact-check their own work, that the cognitive capacities of LLMs are severely limited.
statement.document_title: LLMs aren’t very bright. Why are so many people fooled?

from_speaker: "utter inability to fact-check their own work"
"the cognitive capacities of LLMs are severely limited"
our_interpretation: The core claim is a broad judgment that LLM 'cognitive capacities' are 'severely limited'. He names no task, benchmark, model or threshold, and there is no agreed measure of 'cognitive capacity' that would mark 'severely limited' versus not.

The supporting premises (LLMs make errors, hallucinate, and struggle to check their own work) were checkable in April 2024. But they are offered as reasons for the judgment. They are not the judgment itself, and the same facts sit alongside strong benchmark results that others read the opposite way.
If it were graded, the period would be the state of LLMs around the post date (early 2024).
criteria.support_condition: Would need an agreed, measurable standard for 'severely limited cognitive capacities' that LLMs of early 2024 clearly fell below. No such standard exists, so this is not scorable.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would need an agreed standard showing LLMs of early 2024 clearly met or beat a non-limited level of cognitive capacity. No such standard exists, so this is not scorable.

evidence.excerpt: LLMs struggle to self-correct their responses without external feedback, and at times, their performance even degrades after self-correction.
evidence.explanation: Backs the narrower premise that LLMs had trouble checking and correcting their own reasoning around the post date. It does not establish the broad judgment of 'severely limited cognitive capacities'.

evidence.excerpt: While less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios, GPT-4 exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks, including passing a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers.
evidence.explanation: Shows the mixed picture. The developer reports both limits ('less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios') and strong benchmark results. Whether this adds up to 'severely limited' is a matter of judgment.
